prompt: A software company wants to set the price for a new analytics add-on. The candidate's framework: (1) Engineering time needed to develop it; (2) Value the add-on creates for customers; (3) Prices of competing analytics tools; (4) Cost to build and support the add-on. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.feedback: Support cost is already in bucket 4, which covers the cost to build and support the add-on. The flaw is that bucket 1 repeats part of bucket 4.

options.text: Buckets 1 and 4 overlap: engineering time is a building cost
options.feedback: Right. Engineering time is the main cost of building the add-on, so bucket 1 is a slice of bucket 4. Use the slot for fit with the current price tiers.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: the add-on has no exact equivalent
options.feedback: Customers compare against the closest tools they could buy instead, so competing prices still anchor what they will pay.

options.text: It's a generic cost-plus approach: it prices from cost, not value
options.feedback: The framework includes value to customers (bucket 2) and competitors' prices. It isn't cost-plus. The flaw is the repeated cost bucket.

explanation: Engineering time is a slice of the cost to build, so bucket 1 repeats bucket 4. Better: customer value, competing tools' prices, the cost floor, and fit with the current price tiers (will it pull customers down from a higher tier?).

extras.corrected_framework: Customer value; competing tools' prices; cost floor; fit with existing tiers and cannibalization
